Ukrainian Drone Strike Disables Several Modules at Yandex Data Center in Kaluga, Company Says — Ukrainian drones struck Yandex data centers in Russia’s Ryazan and Kaluga oblasts on Oct. 8 and 9, disabling equipment and disrupting online services used by Russian companies, including Russian Railways and telecom operator MegaFon.

African Nations Seek Return of Citizens Captured Fighting for Russia in Ukraine — Kenya and Botswana are seeking the return of citizens held in Ukraine, saying some were promised civilian jobs before being forced to serve in Russia’s military. Ukraine estimates that at least 1,700 African nationals have fought for Russia, while some captured by Kyiv have previously told Kyiv Post they were sent to the front under false pretenses.

Russia Lifts Quarantine as WHO Seeks Plague Answers — Authorities in Russia’s Irkutsk region lifted quarantine measures imposed after the unexplained death of a 28-year-old employee of an anti-plague institute. Russia Steps Up Production of Improved Su-34 ‘Fullback’ Bombers — Russia’s Aerospace Forces received an unspecified number of Su-34 fighter bombers on Wednesday, Oct. 7 – the second such delivery in 2026. The company is said to have delivered 18 airframes spreaded through seven batches in 2025 despite foreign sanctions.

Ukraine Strikes Russian Missile Fuel Plant, Oil Depot, Yandex Data Center as Moscow Claims 505 Drones Downed — Ukrainian drones struck a Russian chemical plant producing cruise missile fuel, damaged a Yandex data center in Kaluga for the second consecutive day and reportedly sparked a fire at an oil depot near Belgorod. Moscow claimed its air defenses downed 505 Ukrainian drones overnight.

Austria Releases Ukrainian Investigative Journalist Mykhailo Tkach After Detention in Vienna — Austrian police detained Ukrainian investigative journalist Mykhailo Tkach and cameraman Yaroslav Bondarenko in Vienna while on assignment. Ukrainska Pravda, their employer, demanded their release. Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry sought explanations and consular access, but no charges were announced.

Klitschko Warns Kyiv Faces a Fight for Survival as Russian Strikes Threaten Winter Preparations — Kyiv Mayor Klitschko warned that intensified Russian strikes on bridges and energy infrastructure are threatening the capital’s preparations for winter. He urged residents with family outside the city to consider temporarily relocating as authorities prepare backup heating and supplies.

Trump May Leave 100,000 Ukrainians in US Immigration Limbo Rather Than Renew Protections — The Trump administration faces an Oct. 19 deadline to decide the fate of temporary protected status for more than 100,000 Ukrainians in the US. Lawmakers are weighing a possible 6-month extension through inaction, though it could leave recipients in legal limbo.

US, Ukrainian Delegations to Discuss Peace in Miami as Trump’s Envoys May Return to Moscow — US and Ukrainian delegations will meet in Miami to discuss new peace proposals, including a possible ceasefire covering energy infrastructure and grain shipments. Baku’s  intelligence cooperation with Moscow and secret German-Russian meetings in Azerbaijan raise questions about potential risks to Ukraine and NATO allies, although no Russian role in the alleged espionage has been established.

Ukrainian Child Rescue Advocate Among Nobel Peace Prize Contenders as Trump Eyes Award — The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize will be announced in Oslo on Friday, Oct. 9, with Ukrainian child rescue advocate Mykola Kuleba among the potential contenders identified by experts. Humanitarian organizations, press freedom advocates and international justice institutions are also being discussed.

Russian Strike Near Apartment Building in Zaporizhzhia Kills 1, Injures 7 — One man was killed and 7 people wounded after a Russian strike near a high-rise residential building in Zaporizhzhia early Friday, Oct. 9.

Putin, Pezeshkian Talk ‘Peace’ in Turkmenistan While Fueling War in Ukraine — Putin and Pezeshkian reaffirmed their strategic partnership during an Oct. 8 meeting in Turkmenistan. Putin pledged support for Tehran, while Pezeshkian criticized US foreign policy and discussed revised peace proposals.

Russia Launches Fresh Wave of Deadly Attacks Across Ukraine – Kyiv Under Drone Threat — Russia launched another overnight assault Friday, Oct. 9, killing a man in Zaporizhzhia and threatening Kyiv with jet-powered drones. Regional authorities reported fresh injuries as Russian guided-bomb and drone attacks continued.

Russian Drone Attack Kills Civilian in Western Ukraine’s Ivano-Frankivsk — A Russian drone attack on Ivano-Frankivsk late Thursday killed a 67-year-old civilian. Regional authorities reported falling drone debris and a fire, while the city’s mayor confirmed the victim was a security guard.

UK Announces $71M Winter Aid, New Sanctions on Russia — UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced £54 million ($71 million) in winter energy and humanitarian aid for Ukraine, while also revealing around 40 new sanctions on Russia during his first visit to Ukraine as foreign secretary on Thursday, Oct. 8. A “Muslim NATO” Just Activated Its Own Article 5 — For the first time in history, an Article 5-style collective defense agreement has been activated outside of NATO.

Zelensky Visits Pryluky With UK’s Miliband, Thanks EU for €1.2B Tranche for Drones — President Volodymyr Zelensky visited Pryluky with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband on Thursday, Oct. 8, after a Russian barrage left 22 civilians dead, including five children. The president ordered housing aid and shelter inspections, while separately thanking the EU for a €1.2 billion ($1.4 billion) tranche that Kyiv aims to spend on air defense, particularly drones, ahead of winter.

Trump Envoys in Talks With Putin’s Money Man Over Russian Gas, Reports Say — Senior US envoy Jared Kushner and Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev have reportedly discussed bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream gas pipelines, five sources familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday, Oct. 8. The pipelines remain under both US and EU sanctions due to Russia’s war in Ukraine, and Germany strongly opposes reopening them.

Ukraine’s Spec Ops Hit Omsk Oil Refinery 2,500 km Away – Again — Ukraine’s SSO says it struck the Omsk Oil Refinery for the second time, with drones traveling nearly 3,000 km (1,864 miles). Trump ‘Can And Should’ Do More: Zelensky Slams US-Russia Business Talks — Ukrainian negotiators will visit the United States on Oct. 9–10, President Volodymyr Zelensky said during a visit to Pryluky following a deadly Russian strike. How to Build a Business Despite the War and Where to Find the Strength: Takeaways From the Fourth Forbes Ukraine CEO Summit — Ukrainian business leaders at the fourth Forbes Ukraine CEO Summit in Kyiv shared strategies for sustaining companies, teams and themselves through the war, from decentralizing operations to supporting employee wellbeing and building resilient organizations.

Shadow Tanker Hit by Ukrainian Drones Threatens Spill Off Russia's Black Sea Coast — A Ukrainian drone strike set the 107,000-ton Aframax Rio ablaze 30 km (15 nautical miles) off Sochi. WATCH: Downed Russian Jet Drone Crashes Near Kyiv Cars — Dramatic footage published by a local Telegram channel appears to show a downed Russian jet-powered drone falling beside cars in Kyiv. Officials have not confirmed the precise location or reported whether the incident caused casualties.

Putin Tells Tehran Ready to Help Mediate Middle East War: Iran State Media — Russian President Vladimir Putin told Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian that Moscow is ready to help mediate the Middle East war, Iranian state media reported. EU Backs Record Sanctions List of 1,646 Russian Targets — EU ambassadors approved proposed sanctions against 743 individuals and 826 entities linked to Russia’s military-industrial complex, as well as 77 people purportedly elected to the State Duma from occupied Ukrainian territories. Putin’s Focus is Now French Elections — Russia is shifting toward an economic war designed to exhaust Ukraine and weaken European support. With the war potentially extending into 2028 and Ukraine facing a $32 billion financing gap in 2027, Europe should secure long-term funding now.

Russian Attack Leaves Unexploded Ballistic Missile Among Homes in Kyiv, Hits Film Studio and Bird Center — An unexploded Russian ballistic missile was found among residential buildings in Kyiv, prompting a complex demining operation.
